questions.questionText: While working as a Director I in a school preparing a quality assurance visit, colleagues report that lesson observation feedback is delayed. Which response best reflects sound educational law and policy judgement?
options: Assuming a draft is enacted law
Applying a rule outside its scope
Checking the current official text and scope of a legal instrument
Relying on a paraphrase without verification
questions.explanation: Checking the current official text and scope of a legal instrument is best because it applies educational law and policy standards with practical steps that protect learning quality, fairness, and evidence-informed action. This is an original GigaLearn practice item — not an official GES examination question. Learning takeaway: in educational law and policy, choose the option that uses evidence, protects learners, and follows fair professional process — not shortcuts that hide problems.
optionExplanations: Incorrect — Assuming a draft is enacted law: it does not apply the educational law and policy principle required here and would weaken fair, evidence-informed support for learners or staff.
Incorrect — Applying a rule outside its scope: it does not apply the educational law and policy principle required here and would weaken fair, evidence-informed support for learners or staff.

Correct — Checking the current official text and scope of a legal instrument: it applies educational law and policy standards with practical steps that protect learning quality, fairness, and evidence-informed action.

Incorrect — Relying on a paraphrase without verification: it does not apply the educational law and policy principle required here and would weaken fair, evidence-informed support for learners or staff.
